The Almighty speaks here in the plural form (innā), which denotes majesty. This is because God exercises His dominion not through a single attribute but through many attributes and diverse perfections: in power, knowledge, wisdom, and His other attributes, glory be to Him.

However, when He speaks of His own essence, He speaks in the singular, as when He says: ﴿Indeed, I am Allah; there is no deity except Me...﴾ [Ta-Ha: 14], thereby affirming His own oneness. When He speaks of one of His acts, He says: ﴿Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder, and indeed, We will be its guardian﴾ [al-Hijr: 9].

We note here that He emphasized the pronoun of the speaker (innā) with (naḥnu), then repeated the pronoun in (nazzalnā) and in ﴿and indeed, We will be its guardian﴾ [al-Hijr: 9]. This is to affirm the importance of the method (manhaj) that the Qur'an brought, that it is a heavenly method from Him, glory be to Him, that it is inimitable for creation, and in this is a declaration of the excellence of the Noble Qur'an.

The root (f-t-ḥ) carries several meanings. We say, fataḥa al-bāb (he opened the door). This meaning indicates the opening of what is closed, and it applies to tangible matters, as in His saying in the story of our master Yusuf, peace be upon him: ﴿And when they opened their goods...﴾ [Yusuf: 65].

There is also a figurative opening in matters that bring good, as in His saying concerning the hypocrites: ﴿Do you speak to them of what Allah has opened to you, so that they may argue with you before your Lord...?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 76], i.e., what He gave you in the Torah of the attributes of the Prophet (ﷺ) mentioned in the Torah. There is also a meaning of fataḥa as: to judge and decide, as in His saying: ﴿Our Lord, decide between us and our people in truth, and You are the best of deciders﴾ [al-A'raf: 89].

Among the meanings of fatḥ is victory, as in the verse before us, by the evidence of His saying after it: ﴿And Allah will help you with a mighty help﴾ [al-Fath: 3], because when the call (da'wah) arose, the disbelievers of Makkah opposed it, plugged their ears against it, and obstinately rejected it, mocking the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and causing pain to him and to those who believed in his call.

The situation was as if the door were closed in the face of the call, so Allah said to him: ﴿Indeed, We have opened for you a clear opening﴾ [al-Fath: 1], i.e., a manifest and evident opening: an opening for the spread of the call and its strength, such that it would have power, might, and protection. After the Quraysh had besieged it in order to eliminate it, He opened the door for it, and it reached the entire Arabian Peninsula; and after the Quraysh had tightened the noose around the call, all the Arabs came to embrace it and defend it.

In another verse He explained to us this matter of opening, saying, glory be to Him: ﴿Do they not see that We come to the land, reducing it from its outskirts? And Allah judges; there is no repeller of His judgment...﴾ [al-Ra'd: 41], meaning He decides for the victory of Islam and its spread across the regions of the earth. When Allah judges and decrees, there is no one to reverse His decree, and no one to overturn His judgment. ﴿Whatever Allah opens to people of mercy, none can withhold it...﴾ [Fatir: 2]. And since Allah has opened, it will not harm you if people close.

The verb (fataḥa) transitively takes its object directly in the tangible sense, as in fataḥa al-bāb, and takes the preposition (lām) as in ﴿Indeed, We have opened for you...﴾ [al-Fath: 1], i.e., We have given you victory, and takes (ʿalā) in matters of meaning, where goods are driven to you by Allah and sent down upon you.

Hence it is commonly said in supplication: fataḥa Allāh ʿalayk (may Allah open upon you), as if goods will descend upon you like rain falling on your head. Of this is His saying, with the difference between the two situations: ﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We opened for them the gates of everything...﴾ [al-An'am: 44], meaning: We brought them good things from every direction ﴿until, when they rejoiced in what they had been given...﴾ [al-An'am: 44], i.e., the rejoicing of insolence and haughtiness, ﴿We seized them suddenly, and they were unaware﴾ [al-A'raf: 95].

Because, as we have said before: if you want to bring down a man, you do not drop him from a mat, for example; rather you raise him up so that the pain is greater. Likewise these people, Allah opened for them the doors of good things from every direction so that they would believe, but they forgot what they were reminded of, so He seized them with the seizure of the Mighty, the Powerful.

When blessing is not met with gratitude, it turns into a calamity: ﴿Nay! Indeed, man transgresses, when he sees himself self-sufficient﴾ [al-'Alaq: 6-7]. And being seized in a state of blessing and comfort is more painful and more grievous than being seized in a state of poverty, for seizure amid blessing is despair after raised hope, like the prisoner who asks for water because of his severe thirst, and the jailer brings him a cup of water until it nears his mouth, then spills it on the ground.

And His saying:

﴿That Allah may forgive you your earlier sins and your later ones...﴾.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 48, verses 2–3:

We have already explained in Surat Muhammad the meaning of "sin" (dhanb) with regard to the Prophet ﷺ, since he is protected from sin (ma'sum). We said that it falls under the category of "the good deeds of the righteous are the sins of those brought near (to God)" (hasanat al-abrar sayyi'at al-muqarrabin). Therefore forgetfulness is counted as a sin in his case, because he is a prophet connected to revelation and entrusted with the method of God, so the forgetfulness that occurs among the rest of his community is not conceivable from him.

For this reason God pardoned them for forgetfulness, whereas He did not pardon it for the Messenger of God. We illustrated this with the forgetfulness of our master Adam: ﴿And We had certainly taken a pledge from Adam before, but he forgot, and We found in him no determination﴾ [Ta-Ha: 115], and this forgetfulness was called a disobedience (ma'siyah).

Thus the forgiveness granted to the Messenger of God concerns matters such as God's rebuke of him: ﴿O Prophet, why do you forbid what God has made lawful for you, seeking the approval of your wives...﴾ [al-Tahrim: 1], and His saying: ﴿We certainly know that what they say grieves you, but it is not you they deny; rather, the wrongdoers reject the signs of God﴾ [al-An'am: 33], and His saying: ﴿Perhaps you will kill yourself with grief over them, if they do not believe in this message﴾ [al-Kahf: 6].

God rebukes His Messenger out of compassion and mercy for him ﷺ, as if He is saying to him: "O Muhammad, do not grieve, and do not burden yourself beyond its capacity, for you have a standing with God." Seeking forgiveness is for such matters, not because he committed a sin involving a violation of the method, far be it from him ﷺ that such a thing should come from him.

The word ﴿that God may forgive you﴾ [al-Fath: 2] derives from "ghafara," and al-ghafr is concealment (satr). Concealing a sin is either by preventing punishment for it after it has occurred, or by concealing the sin before it happens so that it never occurs at all. This is the meaning of ﴿what preceded of your sin and what follows﴾ [al-Fath: 2]: "what preceded" conceals its punishment, and "what follows" conceals the sin itself so that it does not take place.

﴿and complete His favor upon you﴾ [al-Fath: 2]: the completion of God's favor upon the Messenger is that God sent him to all people, for every time and every place. Previous messengers were sent to specific peoples at a specific time, whereas our master, the Messenger of God, came at the appointed moment when the civilizations of the whole world met and the East and West were connected. He came as a universal messenger and the seal of the messages, so we say: "Master of the messengers and seal of the prophets."

Among the completion of the favor is that God opened (the way) for him and removed from before him the obstacles that were hindering the course of the call, until the whole Arabian Peninsula submitted to him and Islam encompassed it. Through him God guided this community, which then carried his message after him and spread it throughout the various corners of the inhabited world.

He drew to himself the two greatest civilizations of that time: the civilization of Persia in the east and the civilization of Rome in the west, to the extent that they say: "Among the wonders of this religion is that it conquered half the globe in half a century, which had never happened before."

God explains to us this matter of completion in His saying: ﴿Today I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you and have approved for you Islam as a religion...﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 3].

For this reason, when our master Abu Bakr heard this verse he said: "Muhammad has announced his own death through this verse," because after completion there is nothing but decline. They took from it an indication of the nearness of the death of the Prophet ﷺ and his passing to the Highest Companion (al-Rafiq al-A'la), to receive the reward.

He chose the proximity of his Lord not as an escape from responsibility but because of his knowledge that the matter had been completed and become stable, and that he had no further task after that, having fulfilled the trust, conveyed the message, advised the community, manifested the affair of the religion, and established its foundations.

As for His saying: ﴿and guide you to a straight path﴾ [al-Fath: 2]: after he saw that the favor had been completed and there were no locks left, he was reassured that God would not abandon him.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and God will help you with a mighty victory﴾ [al-Fath: 3]. Is the victory "mighty" or is it the one helped who is mighty? The one helped is mighty; rather, the victory was described as mighty, as if the victory of truth makes the victory itself happy and honors it, and as if to tell him: by this victory you have obtained what no one like you ever obtained.

In another place God, glorified is He, showed that He helps His Messenger in times of ease, as in the conquest of Mecca, and helps him in times of hardship, as at Hunayn: ﴿God had already given you victory on many occasions, and on the day of Hunayn, when your large numbers pleased you, but they availed you nothing, and the earth constricted for you within its vastness, then you turned back in retreat. Then God sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers and sent down soldiers you did not see and punished those who disbelieved; and that is the recompense of the disbelievers﴾ [al-Tawbah: 25–26].

When they were deceived by numbers, He disciplined them, then He reached them with His mercy and gave them victory. God would not have helped them in the conquest of Mecca and then forsaken them at Hunayn. God was saying to His Messenger: know that God is behind you, your helper and supporter; but you and your community must not be deceived by victory, by strength, or by number: ﴿How often has a small company overcome a large company by permission of God...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 249].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 48, verse 4:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He it is who sent down tranquility (al-sakinah) into the hearts of the believers﴾ [al-Fath: 4], that is, calm and security after the distress had grown severe upon him, and after they had been in humiliation. ﴿And when the eyes swerved, and the hearts reached the throats, and you thought about Allah assumptions﴾ [al-Ahzab: 10], ﴿there the believers were tested and shaken with a severe shaking﴾ [al-Ahzab: 11].

Yes, when distress grows severe it becomes easy, and with hardship comes relief. The heavens intervened and the help of Allah came, ﴿that they might increase in faith along with their faith﴾ [al-Fath: 4], and that He might remove from them whatever had mixed with them and stirred within them of conceit in numbers and of violating the rules of soldiery toward Allah, exalted is He.

﴿And to Allah belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-Fath: 4], meaning: do not suppose that you alone are the soldiers of Allah; rather, Allah has many soldiers, ﴿and none knows the soldiers of your Lord except He﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 31]. Among the soldiers of Allah are the angels who "arrange affairs" (al-mudabbirat amran), that is, those who manage the affairs of the universe by the command of Allah. ﴿For him are successive angels before him and behind him, who guard him by the command of Allah﴾ [al-Ra'd: 11]. Allah has sworn by them, saying: ﴿And by those who arrange affairs﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 5]. These are the soldiers of Allah in the heavens.

Yes, Allah has soldiers in the heavens and soldiers in the earth, by which He destroyed the nations who denied. Read: ﴿So each We seized for his sin: among them were those upon whom We sent a storm of pebbles, and among them were those seized by the Cry, and among them those whom We caused the earth to swallow, and among them those whom We drowned﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 40].

All of these are of the soldiers of Allah: the storm of pebbles, the Cry, the swallowing up, the drowning, and others. No one knows these soldiers except Allah, in terms of how they are known and how they are directed to fight the enemies of Allah, because they work in secrecy.

Yet when the Truthful, glorified is He, willed to support His Messenger, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, He did not support him with any of these cosmic signs; rather He supported him with the strength of faith of the believers in him and their steadfastness in facing their enemies. Otherwise they would have said: "Had it not been for the natural phenomena, they would not have been able over us."

But Allah, glorified is He, made the victory attributed in reality to the hidden soldiers, while the outward aspect is attributed to these believers, so that their awe would remain in the hearts of their enemies.

Therefore we read concerning the event of the Hijrah: ﴿If you do not support him, Allah has already supported him when those who disbelieved expelled him, the second of two; when they were in the cave, when he said to his companion, "Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us." So Allah sent down His tranquility upon him and supported him with soldiers you did not see﴾ [al-Tawbah: 40].

So the soldiers of Allah were present in that situation, for the Siddiq said to the Messenger of Allah: "If one of them looked under his feet, he would see us." Thus there were soldiers whose sight was prevented: the pigeon that nested and the spider that spun its threads were none other than soldiers of Allah.

When Suraqah ibn Malik's horse's legs sank into the sand, the sand became a soldier of Allah. More astonishing still, Allah subjected to the service of the disbelievers themselves one who helped complete the Hijrah, namely the guide 'Abd Allah ibn Uraiqit, who was a disbeliever and did not know the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. That is because Allah prevails over His affair: thus the guide of the material (world) guided the guide of meaning!!

And He said: ﴿And know that Allah intervenes between a person and his heart﴾ [al-Anfal: 24]. We say: because the inspiration of the Merciful is not contested or opposed by the inspiration of Satan. We have seen this in the story of Moses' mother, when Allah inspired her to cast him into the sea, although she was a mother who fears for her child, and yet she cast him. We have also seen it in Pharaoh, who was killing the male children of the Children of Israel; Moses came to him in this form, yet he did not doubt his affair and raised him in his house. Allah, exalted is He, is the Lord of hearts, their Creator and Turner of them as He wills, making them accept His judgment without debate.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Allah has always been Knowing and Wise﴾ [al-Fath: 4]: Knowing of His soldiers, and He, glorified is He, is Wise in directing them at specific times and toward specific people. The matter is not a overpowering force without accountability, nor thuggery, nor oppression; exalted is Allah above that, a great exaltation.

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says:

﴿That He may admit the believing men and believing women into gardens...﴾.

It is related that when the verses ﴿Indeed, We have given you a clear victory, that Allah may forgive you your earlier and later sins, complete His favour upon you, and guide you to a straight path﴾ [al-Fath: 1-2] were revealed, the Companions said: "Congratulations to you, O Messenger of Allah! This is what Allah has prepared for you. But what has He prepared for us?" Then the verse was revealed: ﴿That He may admit the believing men and believing women into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever...﴾ [al-Fath: 5]. This is what is for them.

The orientalists (al-mustashriqun, Western scholars of Islam) paused at His words, glorified is He: ﴿and expiate from them their misdeeds...﴾ [al-Fath: 5]. They said: How can He expiate their misdeeds when He has already admitted them to Paradise? They are only admitted to Paradise after their misdeeds have been expiated.

We say: The meaning is that He covers them over, so that they do not spoil their life in Paradise or their standing before their Lord, glorified and exalted is He. Or He conceals them from them so that they forget them and are not ashamed of them, just as when you do good to someone who has wronged you. The more you increase your kindness to him, the more he reproaches himself. Therefore Allah conceals their misdeeds from them, so they do not remember them, lest they spoil for them the pleasure of the bounty they enjoy.

Here there is a point regarding ﴿That He may admit...﴾ [al-Fath: 5]. First, the lam here (lam al-ta'lil, the lam of causation) indicates purpose, as in His words, exalted is He: ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except that they should worship Me﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 56]. So the cause of creation is worship. As for the claim that His acts are not subject to causation, we say: they are not caused by a cause that returns to His benefit, glorified is He, but to the benefit of others. Thus they are subject to causation.

Then He mentioned the believing women here after the believing men. Why did He single them out for mention, when the custom in most verses of the Qur'an is that women are included within rulings under men? As in ﴿O you who have believed...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 104], where He did not say "O believing women," because the woman is contained within the man, and she is not mentioned except when she has a specific ruling of her own. So why did He mention her here?

They said: Because the context is one of speaking about jihad (striving in the way of Allah, including fighting), as evidenced by His words: ﴿and Allah will help you with a mighty help﴾ [al-Fath: 3]. Women do not fight, so the Truthful One, glorified is He, mentioned her to affirm that she has a reward for jihad, and to remove any doubt from her about this matter.

As for His words, glorified is He: ﴿gardens beneath which rivers flow...﴾ [al-Fath: 5], we have already explained that this verse came with the wording ﴿beneath which rivers flow﴾ [al-Tawbah: 100]. This is not a repetition of one meaning; each of them has its own meaning. When water flows from beneath you, you feel reassured of its continuity, for no one can prevent it from you, because it originates in your own possession. Whereas ﴿beneath which rivers flow﴾ [al-Tawbah: 100] may mean that it flows from a place far from you and passes by you, so you fear it may be cut off from you.

His words: ﴿abiding therein﴾ [al-Fath: 5] remove from your soul the fear of losing the bounty. For worldly pleasure, however great, is spoiled for you by the dread that it may escape you or that you may escape it. So Allah reassures you that the bounty of Paradise is lasting, uncut, and eternal, which does not perish. It will not be taken from you, and you will not be taken from it by death.

Therefore He called it a great triumph: ﴿And that is with Allah a great triumph﴾ [al-Fath: 5]. What about when triumph is described as great? What about when all of this is with Allah? Giving is in proportion to the giver. You rejoice and are happy when a great official is pleased with you, for example, and you rejoice when you do good to someone and he gives you a gift or a reward. So how much more when Allah rewards you?

For this reason I always recall the day we went with some ministers to San Francisco and went to a luxurious hotel. Everyone was amazed by its appearance, the beauty of its design, and what it contained of facilities. When I saw the admiration in their eyes, I said to them: Take this as a sign of faith, and say: This is what humans have prepared for humans, so how about what the Lord of humans has prepared for humans?

Consider here the contrast that shows the difference and sets before you a comparison between what Allah has prepared as reward for the believers and what He has prepared for the hypocrites and the disbelievers. Bringing together opposites is one of the methods of the Qur'an so that the contrast may appear, which is why the Arab poet said in describing his beloved:

The face is like the dawn, white-shining,
and the hair is like the night, black-dark.

Two opposites, when they come together, are beautiful,
and the opposite reveals the beauty of its opposite.

We also note here that He mentioned the hypocrite men and hypocrite women before the polytheist men and polytheist women in suffering the punishment. Yes, because the hypocrite is greater in crime than the polytheist. The hypocrite concealed disbelief and displayed faith, so he slipped into the ranks of the believers and gathered under their banner, while in reality he is a stubborn polytheist who plots against the believers under cover.

As for the polytheist, his outward appearance is like his inward state and his enmity is well known, and it is easy for you to take precaution against him. Therefore Allah the Exalted said about the hypocrites: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depth of the Fire, and you will not find for them a helper﴾ [An-Nisa: 145], meaning: they are beneath the polytheists and lower than them.

And His saying: ﴿those who assume about Allah an assumption of evil...﴾ [Al-Fath: 6]. Ẓann (assumption) is passing judgment on a thing without its reality, and when you say "a'ẓunnu kadha" (I think such-and-such) it means you are not certain of it. Less than ẓann is wahm (illusion). But what is the assumption they held, which Allah described as an assumption of evil?

They said: Muhammad will never be victorious over us, ever. Allah the Exalted clarified this meaning in His saying: ﴿Whoever thinks that Allah will not give him victory in this world and the Hereafter, let him extend a rope to the sky and then cut it off, and then see whether his plotting removes that which enrages him﴾ [Al-Hajj: 15].

Meaning: the one who holds this assumption has nothing before him but to extend a rope to the sky and hang on to it like one who is hanged, then cut that rope and see whether this removes his rage.

This assumption concerns Allah the Exalted, and the first of their assumptions about Allah was that they said: He has no existence. Others said: He exists but has a partner. Others said: The Qur'an is not from Allah but from Muhammad. Others denied the resurrection and the Final Hour.

All of this is an assumption of evil about Allah, so the Exalted answers it with an evil punishment, saying: ﴿upon them is the circle of evil...﴾ [Al-Fath: 6]. The dā'ira (circle) is an area with an enclosing boundary, so it is as if they cannot escape from it because it encompasses them.

In another place He said: ﴿and Allah encompasses them from behind them﴾ [Al-Buruj: 20]. Not only this, but also ﴿and Allah became angry with them and cursed them and prepared for them Hell, and evil is the destination﴾ [Al-Fath: 6]. Glory be to Allah, how many kinds of punishment, torment, wrath and curse has He gathered upon them?!

Anger (ghaḍab) is an emotion that stirs the angry one against the one who is angered, so that he takes revenge upon him. The Exalted is free of emotion; rather, He speaks to us according to the measure of our understanding and according to the means of expression available in our language.

﴿and cursed them...﴾ [Al-Fath: 6]: He expelled them from the expanse of His mercy and distanced them from it. Then after that the angels curse them and those who curse curse them. ﴿and prepared for them Hell...﴾ [Al-Fath: 6]: He has prepared it in actuality, so it exists now. ﴿and evil is the destination﴾ [Al-Fath: 6]. And His saying: ﴿upon them is the circle of evil...﴾ [Al-Fath: 6] is the natural recompense for the evil assumption they held about Allah.

Also mentioned here are the armies of Allah, glorified and exalted be He, for they descend in two categories: armies of mercy that descend with good, such as the angels who descend with the revelation (al-tanzil) and with the Revelation (al-wahy), and others with water; and there are armies that descend with vengeance, obliteration, punishment and humiliation.

And we understand from His saying, exalted be He, ﴿And Allah is ever Mighty and Wise﴾ [al-Fath: 7] that the intended meaning of "armies" here is the armies of punishment, for they are the ones that suit the attribute of might (al-'izza). The Mighty (al-'Aziz) is the One who overcomes and is not overcome, and this might is restricted by wisdom (al-hikma), free from tyranny or injustice; exalted is Allah above that, high above all.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 48, verses 8–9:

The address here is to our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), to whom his Lord, exalted is He, says: ﴿Indeed, We have sent you as a witness﴾ [al-Fath: 8]. O Muhammad, ﴿a witness﴾ [al-Fath: 8], i.e., over your community and over those who came before you among the messengers, that they have conveyed the message. Yes, he is a witness over them by what Allah informed him of in the Qur'an.

In another verse, He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And thus We have made you a middle nation, that you may be witnesses over the people and the Messenger may be a witness over you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 143]. That is, you bear witness before the people that you have conveyed the message to them, because this community inherited the call from the Messenger of Allah and carried it after him.

Therefore, a noble hadith has been related of the words of our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and his saying: ﴿and a bearer of good tidings and a warner﴾ [al-Fath: 8], bearing good tidings of good and warning of punishment. We have said that good tidings or warning come before the event occurs. But why a bearer of good tidings and a warner? He said: ﴿That you may believe in Allah and His Messenger, and support him [tu'azzirūhu] and honour him [tuwaqqirūhu] and glorify Him [tusabbihūhu] morning and evening﴾ [al-Fath: 9].

So: the reason for sending is that you may believe in Allah and His Messenger. ﴿And support him﴾ [al-Fath: 9], i.e., magnify him, support his religion, and elevate his word. ﴿And honour him﴾ [al-Fath: 9], i.e., magnify him and esteem him its due esteem, because He, glory be to Him, set for His creation a method that guards the movement of their lives from frivolity.

When Allah created Adam and fashioned him in His form and breathed into him of His spirit, life stirred in him and he came into being as a complete creation, meaning that he was not a child who then grew up and became a youth and then a man.

Rather, life stirred in him while he was a fully mature man. Adam arrived into an existence that Allah had prepared for him, in which were all the sustaining elements of his life: water, air, earth, sun and moon. After He gave him the substance of his material form, He gave him the values which are the sustenance of the spirit.

Therefore, after Allah favoured him with the spirit of matter, He gave him another spirit, that of values: ﴿And thus We have revealed to you a spirit of Our command﴾ [al-Shura: 52]. Therefore the Qur'an was named a spirit, and the angel who brought it down was named a spirit: ﴿The trustworthy Spirit has descended with it﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 193]. And He addressed the living with His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life﴾ [al-Anfal: 24]. Thus it is known that there are two lives: the life of matter and the life of the spirit, which is the method.

The discussion here concerns the Pledge of al-Hudaybiyyah, which took place at the Tree of Good Pleasure (shajarat al-Ridwan), about which Allah said in this same surah: ﴿Certainly Allah was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree. He knew what was in their hearts, so He sent down tranquility upon them and rewarded them with a near victory.﴾ [al-Fath: 18].

So, the victory we are discussing had its first signs in this pledge, at the beginning of the Great Conquest. Therefore, when our master Umar objected and said to the Messenger of Allah: "Why do we accept humiliation in our religion?", as-Siddiq Abu Bakr rebuked him and said: "Hold fast to your stirrup, O Umar." That is, do not overstep your limits, and know your place.

As-Siddiq used to say: "By Allah, there was no conquest in Islam greater than the conquest of al-Hudaybiyyah." Why? Because it paved the way for the conquest of Makkah. But people at that time could not grasp what lay between Muhammad and his Lord, and it is in human nature to be hasty.

As for the Almighty, He does not hasten with the haste of His servants; matters reach what He intends. You know the story of Umm Salama, and the plan of Umm Salama succeeded, and the Muslims were saved from a trial that nearly destroyed them. True, it was a zeal born of faith, and on its surface it pleased the Messenger of Allah, but if the command comes from Allah on high, then it is more deserving of hearing and obedience.

Hence they said: "Courage is to be cowardly for an hour." Suppose we were sitting in a place with our elders and great men, and a criminal entered holding a pistol, ordered us to stand, and threatened us. What would we do? We must comply with his order in that situation so that we do not expose ourselves to danger.

So there is courage toward others and courage toward oneself, and the latter is part of wisdom and statecraft. This is what the Messenger of Allah did, and what he saw, through the light that connected him to the Almighty.

This treaty was an elevation of Islam and a raising of its banner, even though they returned without entering Makkah. That is because the Quraysh had taken Islam as an enemy and did not allow it to express itself, but now they opened the door to dialogue and discussion with it. Thus Islam acquired an entity and a voice that is heard, and it rose above the humiliation and abasement of the past.

Likewise, the treaty brought calm to the Quraysh and removed the resentment and enmity they harbored against the Muslims. By making peace with them, we secure their flank so that we can devote ourselves to spreading the call throughout the rest of the Arabian Peninsula. Before the Muslims reached Madinah on their return journey, the Almighty clarified the matter to His Messenger (ﷺ), saying: ﴿Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you are only pledging allegiance to Allah...﴾ [al-Fath: 10].

The bay'a (pledge) is a contract between two parties and an agreement. Selling (al-bay') is something a person loves, in contrast to buying (ash-shira'). Therefore, Allah the Exalted said concerning Friday: ﴿So hasten to the remembrance of Allah and leave off trade...﴾ [al-Jumu'a: 9], because you love to sell; as for buying, you are not as eager for it as you are for selling, and you may buy while you are unwilling.

So, "they pledge allegiance to you" means they conclude a sales contract with you. Allah the Almighty explained this contract in His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties in exchange for that they will have Paradise...﴾ [at-Tawba: 111].

So they concluded this transaction with Allah: ﴿Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you are only pledging allegiance to Allah...﴾ [al-Fath: 10], because you, O Muhammad, take nothing for yourself; you take only for the methodology of Allah with which He sent you and for which He raised you up.

Thus the pledge to the Messenger is in reality a pledge to Allah. Hence He said: ﴿The hand of Allah is over their hands...﴾ [al-Fath: 10], meaning: above the hands that were extended to pledge allegiance to the Messenger of Allah. So the hand of Allah was above the hand of everyone. The favor here is from Allah, so do not think that the favor is from you because you pledged allegiance. Rather, the favor is from Allah upon you, and His hand is above your hands, for He is the One who brought you this good that makes you happy in this world and in the Hereafter.

The "hand" here is not the hand we know, like our hands; rather, it is the hand of favor and kindness, as when you say, for example: "So-and-so has a hand upon me," meaning: a blessing, a kindness, or a benefaction.

His saying: ﴿Whoever breaks [his oath]...﴾ [al-Fath: 10], meaning: whoever violates his covenant, ﴿then it is only against himself that he breaks it...﴾ [al-Fath: 10]. He is the one harmed, because Allah the Exalted is not harmed by anything the servants do; obedience does not benefit Him, and disobedience does not harm Him.

On the other side: ﴿And whoever fulfills what he has promised Allah...﴾ [al-Fath: 10], meaning: he fulfilled it and was faithful to the covenant he took upon himself, ﴿He will give him a great reward...﴾ [al-Fath: 10].

Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated this story, and that al-Hudaybiyyah is a place about 22 km from Makkah, by a tree that was leaning, and so it was named al-Hudaybiyyah, or by a spring of water from which they drank. Their number was one thousand four hundred. In the narration of al-Bukhari, our master Salama ibn al-Akwa' reported that they pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah unto death; and in the narration of Muslim, that they pledged allegiance to him not to flee from the battle.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 48, verses 11–12:

This is an announcement from Allah, Exalted, of an unseen matter that He reveals to His Prophet (ﷺ), informing him of what these people will say. Al-mukhallafun (those who were left behind) is the plural of mukhallaf, and they are those whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked to set out with him for the performance of ʿUmrah, but they did not go out and afterwards made excuses with these pretexts, whose falsehood the Qur'an exposed, and it revealed their intentions and what was passing through their souls.

Al-aʿrab are the Bedouins and the inhabitants of the desert. Their saying: ﴿Our properties and our families have kept us busy﴾ means: from going out with you.

Their saying: ﴿So ask forgiveness for us﴾ indicates that they had committed sin and error, for otherwise they would not have asked the Messenger of Allah to seek forgiveness for them.

In reality they are liars in this. Their properties did not preoccupy them, nor did their children; rather, they feared for themselves from going out, because they thought that the Messenger of Allah would not return from this ʿUmrah and would not go back to his family, since the Quraysh were lying in wait for him, along with groups of the Ahabish, and of Thaqif, Kinanah and others.

So they said to themselves what Allah informed of: ﴿Nay, you thought that the Messenger and the believers would never return to their families again﴾. Therefore, those who said this were confounded when they heard Allah report it and expose the secrets of their hearts.

What is remarkable is that this announcement, ﴿The ones left behind will say to you﴾, was revealed in a Qur'an that is recited openly, and these left-behind people heard it. It was in their power not to make excuses with these pretexts, but Allah spoke the truth and they did in fact say what the Qur'an had announced.

This is exactly what happened in the matter of the change of the qiblah, in His saying: ﴿The foolish among the people will say: What has turned them away from their qiblah which they were upon?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 142].

The Jews heard this statement and heard this description, and nevertheless they said what Allah had announced and confirmed that they were foolish. This and similar instances are among the signs of the truthfulness of the Noble Qur'an, for the one who speaks it is the One who knows what will happen in the future, announces it before it occurs, and then reality comes exactly in agreement with what was said.

It is said: These left-behind people were from seven tribes, I think, among them Ashjaʿ, Muzaynah, Hawazin, Bakhaʿ, Aslam and others. These said: Muhammad has thrown himself into destruction, and he will not return from this ʿUmrah, because of what they know of the strength confronting him; so they stayed behind, whereas in fact they were wishing to set out for Khaybar, where there were spoils and wealth beyond counting.

His saying: ﴿They say with their tongues what is not in their hearts﴾ [al-Fath: 11], that is, in their saying: ﴿So ask forgiveness for us﴾ [al-Fath: 11]. This word is only on the tongue; they are not concerned with forgiveness and do not think about it.

Then Allah, Exalted, makes the reality of the matter clear to them: ﴿Say﴾ [al-Fath: 11], meaning: Say to them, O Muhammad: ﴿Who then can avail you anything against Allah, if He intends you harm or intends you benefit?﴾ [al-Fath: 11].

This is a question of wonder or of rebuke, saying to them: Who can turn away Allah's decree from you, and who can repel from you the harm, should it befall you in your properties or in your families? Who? No one.

Likewise, no one can withhold benefit from you if Allah intends it for you. Thus this is a false argument that profits nothing, and a lie from which no good comes. ﴿Rather, Allah is ever Acquainted with what you do﴾ [al-Fath: 11], meaning: nothing of your affairs is hidden from Him.

Then He admonishes them by disclosing the words that they had confided to one another, saying: ﴿Nay, you thought that the Messenger would never return to his family﴾ [al-Fath: 12], that is, return ﴿the Messenger and the believers to their families ever﴾ [al-Fath: 12], and they reinforced their assumption because they were convinced of it ﴿and that was made attractive in your hearts﴾ [al-Fath: 12], that is, some of you made it attractive to others, or it met with your approval.

﴿And you assumed an assumption of evil﴾ [al-Fath: 12], that is, the corrupt assumption, meaning that the Messenger would not return to his family nor would the believers with him, and this would mean the end of the course of the call.

﴿And you were a people ruined﴾ [al-Fath: 12], meaning: like barren land in which there is no good; you are like this land, a people of corruption in whom there is no good.

The discussion here contains a clear indication that it refers to these who stayed behind. His saying ﴿We have prepared [it]..﴾ [Al-Fath: 13] means: We have already prepared it, so it exists. The Blaze (al-Sa'ir) is not prepared for them only after they arrive at it. Rather, it has already been prepared for them now, awaiting them and longing for them.

We have previously explained that Allah, the Exalted, prepared the Garden so that it would suffice all of creation, on the basis that they would all be believers. Likewise, He prepared the Fire so that it would suffice all of creation, should they disbelieve.

When the people of the Garden enter the Garden and the people of the Fire enter the Fire, the places of the people of the Fire remain empty in the Garden. Therefore, Allah, the Exalted, bequeaths them to the people of the Garden. This is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Those are the inheritors, who will inherit Paradise; therein they will abide forever.﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 10-11]

Al-Balaghiyyun (the rhetoricians) say: The verse contains a restrictive construction (qasr) by placing the predicate, the prepositional phrase, before the subject: ﴿And to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth...﴾ [al-Fath: 14], meaning: to God alone, and ownership of them is restricted to Him, glory be to Him, with no partner.

The root m-l-k comes with a damma, a fatha, and a kasra on the mim, while the lam is sukun.

We say: mulk with a kasra (mulk) means what one possesses and has the right of disposal over. Mulk with a damma (muluk) belongs to the one who owns a thing, and the owner of a thing possesses it, and this belongs to God, mighty and majestic.

As for malak with a fatha, it means capability (al-maqdirah), as in His saying: ﴿We did not break our promise to you by our own power...﴾ [Ta-Ha: 87], meaning: by our will, but we were compelled.

This verse came here as the container (al-zarf): ﴿And to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth...﴾ [al-Fath: 14], and it came in another place for the contained (al-mazruf): ﴿To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth...﴾ [al-Taghabun: 1], because the heavens and the earth are a container for many things.

It is known that the contained is more precious than the container that holds it, as we have said: what is in the treasury is more precious and more valuable than it, otherwise it would not be kept in it.

So if the heavens and the earth contain wonders that cannot be counted, then what of the creatures of God within them? Here we are, every day scientists discover something new in God's creation, in which there is a miracle.

Take as an example the air, which we used to think was only for the process of breathing. Now we know it is a wide field of sound and light waves, and the ether around us is full of such things without limit.

So: search in the container for the preciousness of the contained. Do we not see them now turning towards the interior of the earth, where there are precious treasures of diamonds, gold, minerals and petroleum... Likewise in the mountains are precious stones, granite, alabaster and marble, and in the seas, in their depths, are pearls and coral.

So ﴿To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth...﴾ [al-Taghabun: 1] contains a directive and an indication to research the contained. But ﴿And to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth...﴾ [al-Fath: 14] contains an indication of the obligation to look and reflect upon the wonders of the heavens and the earth in themselves.

As for His saying: ﴿He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills...﴾ [al-Fath: 14], some understand this verse wrongly. They say: then where is choice? The meaning is that God forgives the believer who has been guided to the path of God, and does not forgive the disbeliever who turned away from the path of God.

So when He says ﴿And God does not guide the disbelieving people﴾ [al-Baqarah: 264], it means He does not guide them because of their disbelief, since the disbeliever's heart is filled with disbelief until there is no room left for faith, because a single space holds only one thing. So he must expel disbelief from his heart before he examines the question of faith.

When his heart is stripped of desire, he debates with himself, compares between disbelief and faith, and then admits what he finds reassuring of them, he will inevitably choose faith. Therefore we say: the disbeliever has left no room for rational debate between himself and himself.

And read in this His saying: ﴿Say: I admonish you with one thing...﴾ [Saba: 46], which is ﴿that you stand before God in pairs and singly, then reflect: there is no madness in your companion...﴾ [Saba: 46].

So: the Truth, glory be to Him, does not approve for us chaotic thinking, nor does He approve for us sterile disputation and argument. Therefore He specified the manner of looking, reflecting and searching: either you are alone and debate yourself, or at most two together, one says and the other corrects him, for they are far from contention and fanaticism, and close to reaching the truth.

Although the verse speaks of forgiveness and punishment ﴿He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills...﴾ [al-Fath: 14], it concludes with forgiveness and mercy, for these are the predominant ones: ﴿And God has always been Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Fath: 14].

Here too, the Almighty declares what those who stayed behind will say. By "the spoils" is meant the spoils of Khaybar. ﴿Let us follow you⦆ [al-Fath: 15] means: that we may take a share of them just as you do. ﴿They wish to change the words of Allah⦆ [al-Fath: 15] means: His ruling upon them that they not go out to it.

The Almighty has made this clear in His saying: ﴿Had they intended to go out, they would have made ready for it some preparation; but Allah disliked their setting out, so He held them back, and it was said, "Sit with those who sit."* Had they gone out among you, they would have added to you nothing but corruption, and they would have hastened about among you, seeking to cause you fitnah, and among you are those who listen to them. And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers⦆ [at-Tawbah: 46-47].

So the "words of Allah" here means His ruling upon them that they not go out to Khaybar. The ruling of Allah cannot be annulled, and the word of Allah cannot be turned back. Allah deferred them to another opportunity, one to come, in which they could take part: the wars of apostasy (ridda).

Then the response to them came: ﴿Say, "You will never follow us; thus has Allah said before"⦆ [al-Fath: 15], that is, before our return. ﴿Then they will say, "Rather, you envy us"⦆ [al-Fath: 15], that is, because we would take a share of the spoils along with you. ﴿But they did not understand except a little⦆ [al-Fath: 15]. Indeed, they understand only a little, because the matter is not a matter of spoils.

The meaning: O group of those who stayed behind from going out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for the ʿUmrah of al-Hudaybiyyah, Allah has prevented you from going out to Khaybar, because there are people who have more right to it than you, and they are those who obeyed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in going out to al-Hudaybiyyah.

As for you, the opportunity lies before you in the wars of apostasy (ḥurūb al-ridda), where you will fight a people ﴿possessed of great might...﴾ [al-Fath: 16], people of strength and experience in war. ﴿And if you turn away...﴾ [al-Fath: 16], that is, you refuse and hold back, ﴿as you turned away before...﴾ [al-Fath: 16], that is, at al-Hudaybiyyah, ﴿He will punish you with a painful punishment﴾ [al-Fath: 16].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 48, verse 17:

That is: there is no sin upon these people, nor any blame for their staying behind from going out to jihad, because they are people of excuse, and they do not have the means of jihad. Then the context places us before this comparison between the action and its recompense: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger...﴾ [An-Nisa: 13], that is, in the command to go out, ﴿He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow; and whoever turns away...﴾ [Al-Fath: 17], that is, turns away, ﴿He will punish him with a painful punishment﴾ [Al-Fath: 17].

This is the Pledge of Good Pleasure (bay'at al-Ridwan), which is the Pledge of al-Hudaybiyah. ﴿So He knew what was in their hearts⦄ — of longing to see the House and to perform the 'umrah. ﴿So He sent down tranquility upon them⦄ — calm and serenity, because they submitted to the command of the Messenger of Allah.

﴿And rewarded them⦄ — He recompensed them. ﴿with a near victory﴾ — and this is the treaty of al-Hudaybiyah, which was in the position of a prelude (tamhid) to the greater victory, the conquest of Makkah. ﴿And much spoils⦄ — these are the spoils of Khaybar.
