**Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So He has hastened this for you﴾ [al-Fath: 20]**, meaning: the spoils of Khaybar. **﴿And He restrained the hands of the people from you...﴾** [al-Fath: 20], meaning: He restrained the hands of your enemies from you, among the Jews and others who were around Madinah, since He cast terror into their hearts.
"I.e., other spoils. What is meant by them is the spoils (*ghanā'im*) of the Battle of Ḥunayn, which God gave them good tidings of in the future, and they indeed came after the conquest."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 48, verses 22–23:

His saying: ﴿They would have turned their backs﴾ [al-Fath: 22], meaning: they would have fled and been routed. ﴿Then they would find no protector or helper﴾ [al-Fath: 22], meaning they would find no friend or supporter. And this is ﴿the way of Allah﴾ [al-Fath: 23], meaning His method and custom in His creation, that He gives victory to the people of truth and forsakes the people of falsehood, ﴿which has already taken place before﴾ [al-Fath: 23], meaning it has passed among the earlier nations.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 48, verses 22–23:

His saying: ﴿They would have turned their backs﴾ [al-Fath: 22], meaning: they would have fled and been routed. ﴿Then they would find no protector or helper﴾ [al-Fath: 22], meaning they would find no friend or supporter. And this is ﴿the way of Allah﴾ [al-Fath: 23], meaning His method and custom in His creation, that He gives victory to the people of truth and forsakes the people of falsehood, ﴿which has already taken place before﴾ [al-Fath: 23], meaning it has passed among the earlier nations.

Bitn Makkah (the valley of Makkah) is a place near al-Hudaybiyah. ﴿After He had given you victory over them…﴾ [al-Fath: 24] — that is, He gave you victory over them and made you prevail over them. This strength is what compelled the disbelievers of Makkah to sit down with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for negotiation. The Muslims had become a voice that is heeded and an opinion that is respected, and so the Quraysh came to conclude a treaty with them.

Almighty Allah explains to them the wisdom behind making peace and not entering into battle with the disbelievers at this time. It is true that they barred you from the Ka'bah and prevented you from entering Makkah, while you longed for the House and had with you the offering (hady) that you were driving to the House.

The hady is a sign of peace, and a sign that you did not come for war, but for a devotional act of worship: ﴿And the offerings, detained from reaching their place of sacrifice...﴾ [al-Fath: 25]. The hady (offering) is the livestock given to the poor of the Haram. ﴿Detained (ma'kufan)﴾ [al-Fath: 25] means restrained and held back for this purpose, and ﴿their place of sacrifice (mahillahu)﴾ [al-Fath: 25] means the place where it is slaughtered.

Then He reveals to us the reality of the people of Makkah at this time. In Makkah there are Muslim brothers of yours who conceal their Islam; among the disbelievers there are believing men and believing women whom you do not know. Had you met them in battle, you would have killed them, while you did not know this fact.

﴿Then there would have befallen you from them a crime without knowledge [of you]﴾ [al-Fath: 25]. Ma'arrah means harm, and it would become a stain upon you that you had killed your brothers.

﴿Had they been apart (tazayyalu)﴾ [al-Fath: 25] means had they separated and been distinguished, the believer from the disbeliever, ﴿We would have punished those who disbelieved among them with a painful punishment﴾ [al-Fath: 25]. That is: We would have punished them at your hands, and We would have permitted you to fight them.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on Surah 48, verse 26:

The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, explains to His Messenger (ﷺ) the reason they barred him from entering Makkah this year. The whole matter was merely spite and jahiliyyah zealotry (ḥamiyyah) that took hold of these people's hearts, so it was grievous to them that Muhammad and his Companions should enter Makkah, for their entering this year would be a humiliation to them.

Ḥamiyyah (zealous pride) is recklessness, conceit and arrogance. Strength is neither praised nor blamed except through its effect on its possessor: strength is praised if it brings its possessor good, and blamed if it drags him into evil and casts him into ruin.

﴿Then Allah sent down His tranquillity (sakīnah) upon His Messenger and upon the believers...﴾ [al-Fath: 26] Sakīnah means calm, trust in Allah's help, contentment with the treaty, and returning without entering Makkah this year.

﴿And He made them hold fast to the word of piety (kalimat al-taqwā)...﴾ [al-Fath: 26] which is the word of monotheism (tawḥīd). ﴿And they were more deserving of it and worthy of it...﴾ [al-Fath: 26] meaning more fitting for it and fit to bear it, since they merited it through their obedience to Allah and His Messenger.

Allah, glorified and exalted, relates to us the story of the Muslims' longing for the House after they had been away from Makkah for a long time. They yearned to perform the 'umrah (the lesser pilgrimage) and to circumambulate the House (tawaf). But the fanatical pride of the Age of Ignorance (hamiyyat al-jahiliyyah), its recklessness, and its arrogance in a false strength stood between them and what they wanted.

When Allah speaks about this matter, He speaks of it as a vision that preceded the actual event. As you know, a vision is what a sleeper sees, and it may come true or it may not.

The Qur'an mentions the vision in the story of Sayyidunā Yūsuf (peace be upon him): ﴿Father, I saw eleven stars, and the sun and the moon; I saw them prostrating to me.﴾ [Yūsuf: 4].

The orientalists paused at this verse and objected to the Qur'an's style in repeating the verb (saw) in this verse: ﴿and the sun and the moon; I saw them prostrating to me.﴾ [Yūsuf: 4].

Whoever reflects on the story and its details will find no repetition, because each of the two occurrences of the verb has its own significance and meaning. The first says: ﴿I saw eleven stars, and the sun and the moon..﴾ [Yūsuf: 4] and does not say "prostrating." In the second he says: ﴿I saw them prostrating to me...﴾ [Yūsuf: 4].

This means that the first vision is other than the second. In the first, he saw them without prostration, in their natural state. Then he saw them in a state of prostration, because you do not know the sun, for example, to be prostrating unless you first knew it not to be prostrating and then prostration came upon it.

Therefore the verb must be repeated here: once for the state without prostration, and once for the prostration, meaning that he was surprised to see it prostrating. Had he said at the outset, "I saw it prostrating," we would have asked, "How?" Because prostration does not occur except through the movement of something still and its moving into prostration.

So Allah, glorified and exalted, does not place a word except for a purpose and a meaning, and for an exact choice of expression that is necessary.

When Yūsuf related this vision to his father, he said: ﴿He said: My son, do not relate your vision to your brothers, lest they plot against you a scheme..﴾ [Yūsuf: 5], because Sayyidunā Ya'qūb (peace be upon him) knew that this vision signified Yūsuf's elevation above his brothers, and that they had already harboured resentment against him because of their father's preference for him and his showing him more affection than them.

So how much more if he were to relate this vision to them? How much more if they knew that the highest realm of creatures had prostrated to him?

Likewise here there is a vision: ﴿Certainly did Allah fulfil the vision for His Messenger in truth..﴾ [al-Fath: 27]. It was as though Sayyidunā Rasūl Allāh (ﷺ) had seen a vision in which ﴿you will surely enter the Sacred Mosque, if Allah wills, secure, having your heads shaved and your hair cut short, not fearing..﴾ [al-Fath: 27].

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) related this vision to his Companions, and they were reassured about entering Makkah and performing the 'umrah. Likewise, when the foolish men of Quraysh prevented them from entering Makkah, they were astonished and objected to being prevented from entering.

Sayyidunā 'Umar said to Sayyidunā Rasūl Allāh: "Are we not upon the truth? Are they not upon falsehood?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then why do we accept humiliation in our religion?"

It is true that they were upon the truth and had come out of longing for the House. But if they entered Makkah by force and without the consent of its people, a battle would break out between them. We have said that it would strike a group of Muslims in Makkah who had not declared their Islam, as mentioned in the preceding verse.

Therefore Allah, glorified and exalted, said, after ﴿He knew what you did not know..﴾ [al-Fath: 27]. Allah informed His Prophet of the vision and confirmed it in reality, but it had not yet occurred, because Allah knows from the reality of the matter what you do not know. Therefore He postponed the 'umrah that year, and made the Messenger conclude a treaty of peace between himself and the unbelievers of Makkah, on condition that they would perform the 'umrah the following year.

Consider His words: ﴿You will surely enter the Sacred Mosque, if Allah wills..﴾ [al-Fath: 27]. He did not specify a time for it. So if someone were to say, "Did you not say that we would perform the 'umrah and enter the Sacred Mosque?", it would be said to him: "Not necessarily this year."

Whoever reflects on the wording of the verse will find that it indicates this meaning, and that the 'umrah would not be this year. We understand this from the meanings of the words ﴿You will surely enter the Sacred Mosque, if Allah wills, secure..﴾ [al-Fath: 27].

If you were to enter without the permission and consent of Quraysh, this security would not be realised for you. They would fight you and attack you. Even if they permitted you to enter, they would not bear the sight of you circumambulating the House, and the fanaticism of the Age of Ignorance would certainly seize them.

Then He said: ﴿having your heads shaved and your hair cut short, not fearing..﴾ [al-Fath: 27]. This is another security, after performing the 'umrah, because when anyone entered the sanctuary (haram) for a rite of worship (nusuk), Quraysh would not confront him, but they would attack him after he had finished his rite.

So His words ﴿not fearing..﴾ [al-Fath: 27] indicate that they would be secure at the beginning of the 'umrah and at its end. This would not be available to them except if they entered with the consent and permission of Quraysh.

The phrase ﴿the vision in truth..﴾ [al-Fath: 27]: "the truth" (al-haqq) is that which is established and does not change. Since Allah showed him the vision, it must come true in reality, because the visions of the prophets are true. The prophethood of Sayyidunā Rasūl Allāh (ﷺ) began, first of all, with true visions, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remained in this stage of visions for six months.

If we compare this period with the twenty-three years that constituted the duration of his mission (ﷺ), we find it to be 1/46 of it. Therefore it was related in the noble hadith, that the beginning of prophethood was with good visions, because they come while a person is asleep, and he has no personal thoughts involving desire or self-interest.

As for His words: ﴿So He made after that an imminent victory..﴾ [al-Fath: 27], meaning: after the treaty of Hudaybiyyah and their return without performing the 'umrah, He made an imminent victory for Islam and the Muslims.

This victory is in several respects. Firstly, the truce with Quraysh and the reconciliation with them. This reconciliation gave an opportunity to spread the call outside Makkah, as the Muslims devoted themselves to that after they had secured the side of Quraysh.

This also means the recognition of Muḥammad and his call, and respect for the covenant with him. Islam came to have a word that was heard after it had been persecuted.

Then this treaty was a source of honour for the Muslims, as He said: ﴿And He made binding on them the word of righteousness, and they were most deserving of it and worthy of it..﴾ [al-Fath: 26]. The word of Allah is the word "there is no god but Allah" (lā ilāha illā Allāh). Therefore He said concerning it: ﴿Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you..﴾ [al-Ḥujurāt: 13]. So nobility lies here. Beware lest you think that when Quraysh bars you from the Sacred Mosque, this means honour for them. No, honour belongs to Allah, and nobility before Allah is through piety, not through recklessness and arrogance in a false strength.

In this treaty, the Messenger (ﷺ) gives us a lesson in political wisdom. He accepted the peace with the unbelievers, and he and his Companions returned without entering Makkah that year, although they were close to it, because in that was the benefit of the Muslims and of Islam. Indeed, during the making of the treaty he gave up things that no one thought he would give up.

When they came to write the treaty, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) dictated to the scribe, who was the Imam 'Alī: "This is what Muḥammad, the Messenger of Allah, has agreed to." Suhayl ibn 'Amr said: "No. If we knew that you were the Messenger of Allah, we would not have fought you or taken this stance." The Messenger of Allah replied: "Rather, write: Muḥammad ibn 'Abd Allāh." He yielded to the opinion of Suhayl ibn 'Amr, but 'Alī objected and said: "Rather, I will write: Rasūl Allāh." The Messenger of Allah said to him: "Write it, and you will be asked for something similar and you will accept it."

Indeed, years passed, and a dispute arose between 'Alī and Mu'āwiyah, and when they reached a settlement, 'Alī said: "Write: This is what 'Alī ibn Abī Ṭālib, Amīr al-Mu'minīn, has agreed to." They objected to the words "Amīr al-Mu'minīn" and said: "If we knew that you were Amīr al-Mu'minīn, we would not have fought you." He agreed to that and wrote: "'Alī ibn Abī Ṭālib." This matter was one of the signs of prophethood.

Also, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) dictated at the beginning of the document: "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate," they refused to write it and said: "We do not recognise this. Rather, write: In Your name, O Allah." The Messenger of Allah, Sayyidunā Rasūl Allāh, agreed to this as well.

All of these were concessions from the Messenger of Allah, made out of consideration for the interest of Islam and the Muslims, within the framework of ﴿He knew what you did not know..﴾ [al-Fath: 27]. The result was ﴿So He made after that an imminent victory..﴾ [al-Fath: 27]. Indeed, after this treaty, conquests followed one after another, once the Muslims were secure from the evil of Quraysh for ten years.

The guidance (al-hudā) is the indication of the path of goodness that leads to the end that makes its follower happy in this world and the Hereafter. Our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), was sent with guidance to all people, and so he pointed everyone to it. Whoever is guided by his guidance, Allah helps him and increases him in guidance: ﴿And those who accept guidance - He increases them in guidance and gives them their righteousness﴾ [Muhammad: 17]. Whoever turns away from it and chooses error, Allah increases him in error by sealing his heart.

We may illustrate this with a traffic policeman who directs you to the road. If you hear his words and are guided by his direction, he will accompany you and see you through until he brings you to your destination. If you turn away from him and do not follow his opinion, he leaves you to the difficulties of the road. He may even see you on the wrong road, and he will not advise you, because you did not listen to him.

When the Noble Qur'an spoke of guidance, it said: ﴿Those are upon guidance from their Lord..﴾ [al-Baqarah: 5]. This meaning corrects the mistaken understanding of some who think that guidance is a burden on its bearer, a hardship, an imposition and a restriction of freedom.

But in reality guidance is other than that. Guidance is a mount that carries you to your goal. When you are "upon guidance" (ʿalā hudā), that means you are mounted upon it (mustaʿlin ʿalayhi), riding it so that it brings you to your destination. The method, although in its outward appearance it restricts your movement, restricts it for your own benefit, and it stands against your desires for your own benefit.

When the method restrains your hand from theft, it restrains the hands of all people from stealing from you; and when it commands you to lower your gaze from the forbidden things of others, it commands all people to lower their gaze from your forbidden things. Therefore, you are the winner in this matter. The method restrains your movement from a hasty desire in this world in order to give you lasting bliss in the Hereafter.

As for His saying: ﴿and the religion of truth..﴾ [al-Fath: 28], that is, Islam. Truth (al-ḥaqq) is the established thing that does not change. ﴿that He may make it prevail over all religion..﴾ [al-Fath: 28]: He exalts it and exalts His word over all the religions that preceded it, because the Qur'an came as a guardian (muhayminan) over all these books, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We have revealed to you the Book in truth, confirming that which preceded it of the Scripture and as a guardian over it..﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 48].

The prevailing here is the prevailing of proof and argument, and the prevailing of perfection in its teachings and its method. This does not prevent the existence of other religions, which still exist until now, after fourteen centuries of Islam.

For this reason, we were asked this question during one of our journeys, and we said: ﴿that He may make it prevail over all religion..﴾ [al-Fath: 28] does not mean that all people should become Muslims, because the prevailing here is the prevailing of teachings. This has happened by your own testimony, for the issues of life have driven you to the method of Islam, where you have no solution except in it.

For this reason, we have seen them taking the rulings on divorce in Islam as an example, and this is a manifestation of the religion, because they have adopted its teachings without believing in it. Likewise, regarding the matter of polygamy, they used to attack it and object to it, and now they call for it.

The strange thing is that they accept having a mistress (khalīlah), meaning a lover, but they do not accept having more than one wife (ḥalīlah), meaning a spouse. This is corruption in nature and taste, and a conduct that the laws reject.

Likewise, in the economic aspect: when Kinz, the king of economics among them, spoke, he concluded that money does not perform its social function in the universe unless interest falls to zero. This is the opinion of Islam.

For this reason, Islam forbade dealing in usury (ribā), because usury is a transaction between a rich person and a poor person: the rich one has a surplus that he lends, and the poor one is destitute and borrows. How can we ask the poor man, who does not own the principal, to give the rich man, who owns the principal, plus an increase?

Then suppose the poor man took the money to invest it in trade, and then this trade lost. Then it would be required of him to repay the capital and then the interest, in addition to his effort that went in vain throughout the period of the trade.

So how many calamities have befallen him? Thus the prohibition of usury first considers the interest of the poor man, and also considers the interest of the rich man in everything, because if you are able and you lend, you look to the condition of the rich man.

But circumstances may change, and the rich man may become poor and need to borrow. Therefore, it is not in his interest to deal in usury.

As for His saying: ﴿And sufficient is Allah as Witness﴾ [al-Fath: 28], it means: His testimony is sufficient, because a witness, when he testifies, testifies to what he has seen, and his sight is limited; but when Allah testifies, it is the testimony of all-encompassing knowledge, encompassing completely, and no one can change it. But "as a witness" (shahīdan), upon what? They said: upon the fact that whoever follows the guidance, his destination is Paradise, which is the abode of everlasting bliss that does not end, and the favour that does not cease.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 48, verse 29 (part 1 of 2):

﴿Muhammad﴾ is his name, peace and blessings be upon him. ﴿the Messenger of Allah...﴾ [al-Fath: 29] is his new description, because we knew Muhammad first, before he became the Messenger of Allah. Muhammad, from al-hamd (praise), means that people praise him, and his people praised him from his youth and said: "the Truthful, the Trustworthy" (al-Sadiq al-Amin).

His conduct and his past among them indicated these qualities, and that he was a person distinguished among his peers and not ordinary.

They agreed upon this even before the Message. In his childhood they saw that he was untouched by the frivolity, play and games of childhood. They saw that he herded sheep, like other youths who herd sheep in the desert and who would descend at night to Makkah to attend nights of entertainment.

As for him, he once thought of going down with them, but when he went with them there, sleep overcame him, and he did not wake until the gathering had dispersed. It was as if Allah protected him and purified his hearing and sight from hearing or seeing anything of this. As for his companions, they were astonished that they had not seen him among them. Therefore he became trusted among them, and since they had never tested him in a lie, he became worthy that they should call him: "the Truthful, the Trustworthy."

One day the boys gathered to carry a heavy stone with which they were playing. When it became heavy for them, they rolled up their garments so that the stone would not affect their shoulders. The Messenger of Allah was with them, and he took hold of his garment and wanted to do as they did, but he heard a voice saying to him: "Your private part, O Muhammad!" So he was the only one who did not uncover his private part.

They noticed this about him before the age of discernment, and they took from him the idea that he was prepared from another direction. Then they recognised the soundness of his judgement and the excellence of his thinking in the matter of placing the Black Stone in its place, when the tribes of Quraysh disputed over who would obtain the honour of placing the stone in its place, to the point that they nearly fought one another. Then they said: "Let us make the first one who enters upon us the judge."

So Muhammad, the Truthful, the Trustworthy, about whose trustworthiness no two people disagreed, took his cloak and placed the stone upon it, and commanded each tribe to take hold of a side of it, until, when they had brought it to its place in the Ka'bah, he lifted it and placed it in its position, and thus the dispute that had stirred the anger of the people ended.

So His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Muhammad...﴾ [al-Fath: 29] means: this is the one you know, and you know his truthfulness, his trustworthiness and the nobility of his character. This one who dwelt among you for forty years is the Messenger of Allah whom Allah chose for the Message. Therefore: you witnessed for him before I sent him to you, and since you have testified to him with beautiful character and soundness of judgement, it is obligatory upon you to believe him.

The Truth, glory be to Him, did not describe Muhammad only in his own person; rather He purified his origins and attested to their purity by protecting them from prostrating to idols, which was a worship widespread at that time. They agreed that none of his forefathers had prostrated to an idol.

Therefore there came in the noble hadith: that is, that he, peace and blessings be upon him, came from a pure lineage that was not touched by any of the fornication of the Jahiliyyah.

The story of his father Abdullah with Zaynab al-Khath'amiyyah is well known throughout the whole of the Arabian Peninsula, especially in Makkah, where she saw in him beauty and majesty, so she fell in love with him until she sought to seduce him. At that he said the famous verses:

"As for the forbidden, death is before it,
and the lawful—there is no lawful, so seek clarity.
The noble guards his honour and his religion;
so how about the matter you seek?"

When Abdullah married Aminah bint Wahb and she conceived the Messenger of Allah, that light which had been on the face of Abdullah passed to her. Then when the Khath'amiyyah saw him after that, she said: "What shall I do with him, when the light that was on his face has gone?"

This means that the Truth, glory be to Him, made Muhammad under His own eye, protected him from the fornication of the Jahiliyyah, and protected him at every stage.

After that his father died, and he was nursed among the Banu Sa'd. His wet-nurse saw many marvels and miracles from him. When she said to his foster-brothers: "Protect Muhammad from the heat of the sun," they said: "By Allah, O mother, we never find it hot where he is, for when he walks we see a cloud above him shading him."

So: he was witnessed to in his own person, and witnessed to in his forefathers; everyone knew that he was supported from on high.

So His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah...﴾ [al-Fath: 29] means that He chose the Messenger in accordance with your own opinion, so beware of denying him. Here "Muhammad" is the subject (mubtada'), and what is predicated of him is His saying: ﴿the Messenger of Allah...﴾ [al-Fath: 29].

That is: Muhammad, whom you know, is the Messenger of Allah, and Allah knows best where to place His message. So it was obligatory, at the moment he was sent to you, that you believe in him and affirm him.

When the Truth, glory be to Him, supported Muhammad with miracles, He supported him with a rational miracle, and He distinguished between a rational miracle and a cosmic miracle. The cosmic miracle occurs once, as we saw in the story of our master Jesus, peace be upon him, when he spoke to the people in the cradle; and none saw this miracle except the people who were present and witnessed that situation.

As for us, it is a report that we affirm and believe in, because the Qur'an has informed us of it.

As for Muhammad, his message is general and the seal of the messages until the Hour. Therefore his miracle must be commensurate with the universality of the message; it must be an everlasting miracle that does not end with the end of the occasion.

Therefore the Qur'an came as a miracle that remains as long as the message remains until the Hour. Since the message was revealed, we have been reciting ﴿Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah...﴾ [al-Fath: 29], and it will continue to be recited until the Hour: Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, by the evidence of this miraculous Qur'an.

Therefore He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder, and indeed, We will be its guardian﴾ [al-Hijr: 9]. So the Truth, glory be to Him, Himself took charge of preserving the Qur'an, unlike the earlier books, whose preservation He entrusted to their people and to those who believed in them. ﴿And the rabbis and the scholars, by what they were entrusted with of the Book of Allah...﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 44]. The meaning of ﴿they were entrusted...﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 44] is: they were asked to preserve it as a duty from Allah, and a duty is liable to be obeyed or disobeyed; and we have seen that they did not keep it but altered and changed it and forgot much of it.

As for the Qur'an, it has remained as it is since Allah sent it down upon the heart of His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, because Allah preserved it by His own preservation, and did not entrust that to human beings.

Among the signs of Allah's preservation of the Qur'an is that He has made to serve it those who serve it even from among those who do not believe in it. Many of those who now oversee the printing and decoration of the Qur'an are non-Muslims, and we have seen the German man who printed the entire Qur'an on a single page, although he did not do this with the Gospel, which is his own book.

So we say: the past of the Messenger of Allah among his people qualified him for the mission of the Message. Therefore those who received the news of his mission, peace and blessings be upon him, hastened to affirm him before they heard a single verse of the Qur'an. Why?

Because they took the proof of his truthfulness from his past among them; they had never tested him in a lie, and whoever does not lie to people all the more does not lie against Allah, the Lord of people.

We see a similar stance from the Siddiq, Abu Bakr, in the incident of the Isra' and the Mi'raj: when it reached him that the Messenger of Allah claimed that he had been taken on a night journey, he said: "If he said it, then he has spoken the truth."

As for the miracle, it came for the one who denied and rejected his message, peace and blessings be upon him. It came for the one who did not believe and who accused the Qur'an of being a lie and a fabrication, so it came to say to them: ﴿Then bring a surah like it...﴾ [Yunus: 38], that is, fabricated.

His saying: ﴿and those who are with him...﴾ [al-Fath: 29] means: those who believed in him and did righteous deeds in his company, in their human and methodological companionship. He described these as ﴿severe against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves...﴾ [al-Fath: 29]. So they combined a thing and its opposite: severity and mercy.

This is evidence that the believer does not have a single disposition governing him; rather it changes according to the duty that comes to him from his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic. With enemies you find him strong and severe against them, showing them that the believer's cane does not bend; while with his believing brothers he is merciful to them and tender toward them.

In another place the Qur'an expressed this meaning, saying: ﴿humble toward the believers, mighty against the disbelievers...﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 54]. So the methodology of faith is what governs and directs the believer's conduct, and this is what we have indeed seen in the behaviour of both Abu Bakr the Siddiq and 'Umar the Faruq.

Abu Bakr, despite what was known of him of gentleness and mercy, when the matter of apostasy came after the death of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, we saw him depart from that gentle disposition and become at the utmost of severity.

He said to 'Umar: "By Allah, if they withhold from me a 'iqal that they used to pay to the Messenger of Allah, I would fight them over it." 'Umar rebuked him and said: "A tyrant in the Jahiliyyah, a weakling in Islam!"

Whoever reflects on the matter of apostasy finds that it requires harshness and firmness, otherwise it would spread, especially among the weak in faith, while people were still recent in their adherence to the religion. This is what moved Abu Bakr from a disposition of gentleness to a disposition of severity.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿You see them bowing and prostrating, seeking bounty from Allah and His good pleasure...﴾ [al-Fath: 29]. So, despite this severity toward the disbelievers, you see them bowing and prostrating. Bowing and prostration are stages for displaying complete servitude to Allah, exalted is He: in bowing you incline your stature before Allah, and prostration is greater than bowing, where you fall to the ground and place your forehead, which is the most noble part of you, upon the earth, in humility and submission to Allah and submission to Him, glory be to Him.

Therefore we said: in bowing and prostration is the perfection of servitude to Allah. We understood this from the words of Iblis which the Qur'an relates from him: ﴿Then I will surely come to them from before them and from behind them, and from their right and from their left...﴾ [al-A'raf: 17].

He did not mention the other directions, above and below. Why? Because the above represents the loftiness of divinity, when we raise our hands in supplication, and the below represents the humiliation of servitude, when the foreheads prostrate and submit to Allah, exalted is He. Therefore Satan does not come from these two.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿seeking bounty from Allah and His good pleasure...﴾ [al-Fath: 29]. This is the reason for their being severe against the disbelievers and merciful among themselves, and for their maintaining bowing and prostration: that is, they do this seeking Allah's bounty and hoping for His good pleasure toward them.

This is the peak of sincerity in deeds: their goal in action is the Face of Allah; they look to nothing else. Why? Because they reckon with this Day on which they will stand before Allah, and they find none other than Allah to call them to account and recompense them.

Therefore we said regarding scholars and inventors who served humanity by their good works, and yet have no share in the Hereafter, because they did not work for Allah but for humanity and for civilisation.

Therefore Allah said of them: ﴿And those who disbelieve, their deeds are like a mirage in a level plain, which the thirsty one thinks is water; until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing, and finds Allah with him, and He pays him his account in full. And Allah is swift in reckoning﴾ [al-Nur: 39]. He is surprised by the true God, whom he had not had in mind, Who is the One who reckons with him and recompenses him.

Among the marks of these believers too: ﴿their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration...﴾ [al-Fath: 29]. Their mark, that is their distinguishing sign, is the trace that prostration leaves on a person's forehead, which we call the "prayer mark" (zabibat al-salah).

The Creator, glory be to Him, did not create mankind in the universe on a single mould; rather every person has his own particular mould, which does not match another mould despite the multitude of creation. This is from the freedom of power in the process of creation: people differ in height, shortness, breadth, colour, features, and so on.

But the distinguishing characteristic of all the believers whom Allah described with these attributes is: ﴿their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration...﴾ [al-Fath: 29]. This mark is accompanied by a light in the face and a cheerfulness we notice on the face of the believer, and the servant is nearest to his Lord when he is prostrating.

Many of us find pleasure in prolonging prostration, and find in it intimacy with Allah, and become accustomed to it; so this mark appears on his forehead, along with that light and radiance that appears on his face.

You can notice this if you compare a man who has spent his night in drinking, debauchery and recklessness with another who has spent his night in the worship of Allah and His glorification.

Such faces come thus: ﴿Faces on that Day will be radiant, laughing, joyful; and faces on that Day will have dust upon them, covered with darkness; those are the disbelievers, the wicked﴾ [Abasa: 38–42].

We observe this image, and we see its beginning in this world before the Hereafter.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That is...﴾ [al-Fath: 29] refers to the attributes already mentioned of the believers with Muhammad: ﴿severe against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves; you see them bowing and prostrating, seeking bounty from Allah and His good pleasure; their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration...﴾ [al-Fath: 29]. These attributes are: ﴿their likeness in the Torah...﴾ [al-Fath: 29]. Thus the Torah described them, as if the Torah contains mention and a likeness of the believers who believe in Muhammad, the final Messenger, because the Torah gives good news of him.

As for the Gospel, it described them with other attributes than these: ﴿and their likeness in the Gospel is like a seed that sends out its shoot, then strengthens it, so it grows thick and stands firm upon its stalk, pleasing the sowers, that He may enrage the disbelievers by them...﴾ [al-Fath: 29].

So these believers, in the Gospel, are like a plant that sent out its ﴿shoot [sha'ath]...﴾ [al-Fath: 29], that is, its branches; and the shoot is the top of the stalk or the ear. ﴿Then it strengthened...﴾ [al-Fath: 29], meaning: the stalk grew firm, became strong and filled out. ﴿Then it stood upon its stalk...﴾ [al-Fath: 29], meaning: it reached its full measure, to the extent that it ﴿pleases the sowers...﴾ [al-Fath: 29] because of its perfect uprightness and straightness, ﴿that He may enrage the disbelievers by them...﴾ [al-Fath: 29].

Now you may compare these two examples: you will find that the first example, in the Torah, is concerned with spiritual aspects, and mentions matters and attributes that are all values and immaterial things. The followers of Muhammad are severe against the disbelievers and merciful among themselves; they bow and prostrate, seeking bounty from Allah and good pleasure; their mark is on their faces from the trace of prostration. All of these are values and immaterial things, with nothing material in them at all.

As for their likeness in the Gospel, it is a material image entirely devoid of spiritual matters or values. Why? They said: because the Jews were a materialistic people, excessive in it, such that they would not be convinced except by it.

In the period of wandering in the wilderness that Allah decreed for them, He provided them with manna and quails, a sweet and delicious food that came to them without toil and descended upon them without any effort on their part. But they were not pleased with it, because it was unseen and they did not know its source, and they asked Allah to provide them with what the earth grows of its herbs, its cucumbers, its garlic, its lentils and its onions: that is, what they sow with their hands and handle with their own selves.

Even in their relationship with Allah they wanted Him to be material. They said to Moses, peace be upon him: ﴿We will not believe you until we see Allah openly...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 55]. Yet the Truth, glory be to Him, is unseen: ﴿Vision does not grasp Him, but He grasps vision...﴾ [al-An'am: 103].

As for our seeing Him, glory be to Him, in the Hereafter, it is because we will be prepared there with another preparation befitting that honour, such that we will be able to see Him, exalted is He. In this world we cannot do so, because Allah, exalted is He, has not prevented His manifestation to His creation; but we in this world cannot bear that manifestation.

This meaning is clear in the story of Prophet Musa (peace be upon him), when he said to his Lord, may He be exalted, ﴿My Lord, show me Yourself, that I may look upon You﴾ [Al-A'raf: 143]. The answer was ﴿He said: "You will not see Me, but look at the mountain. If it remains firm in its place, then you will see Me"﴾ [Al-A'raf: 143]. This means that others could see Him. ﴿So when his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, He made it crumble to dust, and Musa fell down unconscious﴾ [Al-A'raf: 143]. When our Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, the mountain crumbled. How much more so, then, if He, glorified and exalted, were to manifest Himself to a human being? Musa, peace be upon him, saw the mountain crumbling, so he fell down and lost consciousness from the terror of what he saw of the effect of the manifestation upon the one to whom it was shown.

We say: since they were in this state of materialism, there came to them a example full of spiritual and moral values. It is as if the Torah mentioned among the attributes of the believers in Muhammad things that refute the People of the Torah, saying to them: "You have gone to extremes in materialism, and I will bring a Prophet whose community upholds the spiritual values and moral principles that you have neglected."

As for the Christians, they gave precedence to the spiritual. The Gospel itself is entirely spiritual and moral. Therefore, when Prophet Isa (peace be upon him) was asked about a matter of inheritance, he said: "I was not sent to divide inheritances."

This contrast between the Torah and the Gospel led the Jews and the Christians to converge upon a single book, a mixture of the Torah and the Gospel, so that they might combine materialism and spirituality. They named it the Holy Book (al-Kitab al-Muqaddas), and they came together upon it despite the enmity and disagreement between them.

Since the Gospel is described in this way, the example of the believers in it is entirely material, and this is the very thing the Gospel lacks. The Gospel is entirely free of discussion of transactions and of the movement of life. Thus each of the two examples came to remedy a deficiency: the Jews lack the spiritual, and the Christians lack the material in the movement of life.

We pause here at His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿that He may enrage the disbelievers by them﴾ [Al-Fath: 29]. This is an indication that our advancement in material things, and our reaching in them the level of balance, uprightness and self-sufficiency, is something that enrages the disbelievers. So beware lest they outstrip you in this field.

If they outstrip you in it, they will humble your necks, take control of your affairs, and dominate you by means of the capabilities they possess that you do not have.

Regrettably, this is what has happened. We have needed them in most industries, even for our daily bread, and see how they treat us! There is no power and no strength except with Allah.

It is as if the Truth, glorified and exalted, is saying to us: "O you who have believed in Muhammad, who have accepted Allah as Lord, Islam as religion, and Muhammad as Prophet, you must take from each of them a share. Take from the material what raises your standing and helps you in the movement of life. And take from the spiritual what protects you from error and sets right your religion and your worldly life, for your example in the Torah is values, and your example in the Gospel is substance."

Therefore Islam came supported by cosmic knowledge that does not contradict it. The Qur'an is full of discussion of these cosmic matters. Read, if you wish, and reflect upon these verses: ﴿Do you not see that Allah sends down water from the sky, and with it We bring forth fruits of varying colors? And among the mountains are streaks, white and red, of varying shades, and deep black. And among men and crawling creatures and cattle are those of varying colors. It is only those of His servants who have knowledge that truly fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Mighty and Forgiving﴾ [Fatir: 27-28].

He mentioned all the kinds of existence: humans, animals, plants and inanimate things. The word "the knowledgeable" here is not limited to scholars of religion; rather, it includes all scholars in every field, whether religious or worldly.

It is as if the Truth, glorified and exalted, wanted for us a religion that combines this world and the Hereafter, worship and the movement of life. So beware lest you take the religion and leave the world to your enemies, who will lead you astray through it.

We have said previously: "Whoever wants his word to reach from his head, let his morsel come from his axe." So beware lest your enemies surpass you in this field, because the bounty of Lordship (rububiyyah, God's sustaining and providing nature) is one for the believer and the disbeliever alike, so do not abandon it relying on the bounty of Divinity (uluhiyyah, the right of worship).

You cannot establish servanthood to Allah unless you take up the bounty of Lordship, and strive to develop the movement of life, benefit from it, and take part in it.

We have previously pointed to the matter of covering the private parts as an example. It is obligatory, and worship is not complete without it. Consider how many movements of life we undertake in order to cover our nakedness with clothing!

Follow the cotton seed from the moment you place it in the ground until it becomes a garment you wear. So we say: the movement of life is what assists the movement of religion.

Then He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿Allah has promised those among them who believe and do righteous deeds forgiveness and a great reward﴾ [Al-Fath: 29]. Note: ﴿who believe﴾ [Al-Fath: 29] is the aspect of religion, and ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾ [Al-Fath: 29] is the aspect of worldly life and what it requires of the movement of life.

So beware, then, of neglecting one aspect for the sake of the other, for your religion is a religion that unites spirit and matter. Those who believed are those who combined these qualities, and Allah promised them this promise.

Faith (iman) is the firm, settled conviction in the soul, which does not admit debate. The heart is at peace with this conviction, and that it makes one happy in this world and the Hereafter. The essence of faith is that you believe in Allah as Lord and Creator of the universe, and you believe in His names and attributes.

When you believe in these attributes, your heart is at rest with whatever He decrees and determines for you. He, glorified, tests you with good that you may give thanks, and tests you with evil that you may be patient, so you are rewarded in both situations.

Faith derives from the root (a-m-n), so its meaning revolves around security and tranquility. You say: "I believed in such-and-such" (amantu bi-kadha), meaning: I held it as a firm conviction that admits no doubt. "I believed him" (amantu lahu) means: I accepted what he said as true. "He gave him security" (amman-hu) means: he reassured him about the future of his life. So all of these revolve around stability, firmness, and not turning into their opposite.

The fruit of faith, ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾ [Al-Fath: 29], is intended by what preceded in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Hard against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves. You see them bowing and prostrating, seeking bounty from Allah and His pleasure. Their mark is on their faces, the trace of prostration﴾ [Al-Fath: 29]. In material matters and the movement of life they are like the seed that has put forth its shoot and stands firm on its stalk, pleasing the farmers, so that through them He may enrage the disbelievers.

And what is the promise to the believers? ﴿Forgiveness and a great reward﴾ [Al-Fath: 29]. We have said: there is a clearing away first, then an adorning. He forgives first, then gives the reward. The legal principle is that repelling harm takes precedence over securing benefit.

Therefore He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿Whoever is spared from the Fire and admitted to Paradise has triumphed﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 185]. Being spared from the Fire is itself a blessing. For this reason the Bridge (sirat) was set up over the back of Hell, so whoever crosses it must see Hell with his own eye: ﴿Then you will surely see it with certainty of sight﴾ [Al-Takathur: 7].

This makes you feel the greatness of faith, and that it is the greatest blessing, because it saved us from this Fire and admitted us to Paradise. And righteous deeds are what took you by the hand and carried you across this obstacle.

Read: ﴿By time, indeed mankind is in loss, except for those who believe and do righteous deeds, and advise one another to truth, and advise one another to patience﴾ [Al-'Asr: 1-3]. So mankind in general is in loss, with no exception, and none are saved except those who believe and do righteous deeds.

Advising one another to truth indicates the obligation of enjoining good and forbidding evil. Advising one another to patience indicates that this path is fraught with dangers and requires patience with harm from opponents and critics, for giving advice is burdensome.

The word ﴿advise one another﴾ [Al-'Asr: 3] means that everyone advises, so it implies continuity, perseverance, and not despairing. Because the opponent you advise may also be patient and persist in his course, you must outlast him in patience. This is the meaning of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who believe, be patient, outdo others in patience, and stand firm﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 200].

The promise of Allah is the true promise that does not fail. Why? Because it is the promise of One who possesses every means of fulfilling it, nothing prevents Him from fulfilling it, and no obstacle stops Him. Moreover, He, glorified, is the Truth who does not change, alter, or transform. So who, then, can stand between Him and the fulfillment of His promise?

He, glorified, is the One God, the One, who has no partner in His dominion and no contender in His authority. He is the Mighty, so no other power can prevent Him. As for the promise of human beings, it may not be fulfilled, because a human does not possess all the means of fulfillment, and he is subject to change and fluctuation.

Therefore He, glorified, says: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves﴾ [Al-Ra'd: 11].

So we say: the Truth, glorified and exalted, is firm and does not change on our account, but it is for us to change ourselves for His sake, may He be exalted.

The word ﴿forgiveness﴾ [Al-Fath: 29] means: the Creator, glorified, who knows best about His creation, knew that we are frequently erring, forgetful, and ignorant. Yet all of this is expected of us, and it should not make us despair of the mercy of Allah, for it is He who created us in this form, and He who has guaranteed us forgiveness. All that is required of us is to knock at its doors: ﴿And indeed, I am Most Forgiving to whoever repents, believes, does righteous deeds, and then remains guided﴾ [Ta-Ha: 82].
